reviewMethod: Independent visual sweep of all 32 paper pages and scheme pages 1–20; each task reconciled against the published mark boundary. All question and answer crops inspected before publication.
sourceNotes: All ten questions retained: 380 offered marks; exam-level choice of five Section A and three Section B questions does not remove any practice question.
40 tasks. Q6(b)(i)–(ii), Q7(a)(i)–(ii), Q7(b)(i)–(ii), and Q8(e)(i)–(ii) share allocations and remain together.
Q1(c) reverses the y values in the printed pairs. Correct pairs are (4, −23/2) and (−6, 17/2). A separately attributed worked example corrects these and retains SEC credit notes.
Q2(b) has a stray j after the final 10 in the scale. The numeric award is 10.
Q3(a) asks for g(f(x)); the correct printed model solution is retained. Credit notes also mention f(g(x)), apparently an alternative partial-credit route, not the requested composition.
Q4(b) has no labelled answer diagram. A NextStepUni schematic labels y=2z, x=−z and w=iz without inventing numeric coordinates in the answer.
Q6(b)(ii) omits the strict lower bound: positivity requires 0<a<3; at a=0 the integral is zero.
Q7(a) prints −925 at x=5 although both the paper and formula give +925, and its graph is omitted. A complete NextStepUni table and graph correct this, retaining the original marking notes.

Four scale labels disagree with their numeric awards. Q7(d): printed 10C (0,3,5,7,10), represented as 10D. Q8(d) and Q10(c): printed 5C (0,2,5), represented as 5B. Q9(d): printed 10D (0,4,6,10), represented as 10C. All numeric awards and original credit notes are preserved, with explicit explanations.
Q8(c) final line should read w′(5), not w′(t). Its −1.06 percentage points per week is expressed as percentage per week in the question.

Q8(e) offers a verbal graph description only. A NextStepUni example with k=−0.15 shows the same initial value 25, a faster decrease, and the same asymptote 5. Any k<−0.079 is valid; this is an open answer, not a finite pool.
Q9(b) asks about f defined on all real numbers. The local maximum at x=8/3 is not restricted to the wave image domain 0≤x≤2. Q9(c) explicitly uses that restricted domain.
Q9(d) prints 0 instead of 1.5 as an intermediate lower integration limit for g. Its actual substituted values and final 25/24 answer are correct; the card note identifies the correct limits.
Q9(e)(ii) is mislabelled (f)(ii) in the summary table; the question and full solution use (e)(ii).
Q10(d)(i) should subtract BC, not CD, to find AC. The numeric calculation 120−96=24 and subsequent AD=100.8 are correct.

cards.stem: A company produces firewood. To make the firewood, the company cuts the wood and then leaves it in a warehouse to dry out. The water content of the wood, w(t), is the percentage of the firewood that is actually water. cards.questionText: Work out the water content of the wood at the start of the drying process, and after 8 weeks. Give each answer as a percentage, correct to the nearest percent where appropriate.

Water is pumped into a container through two pipes. For each pipe, the water is pumped at a constant rate. Pipe A can fill the container in 18 minutes. Pipe B can fill the container in 15 minutes. The container is empty. Water is then pumped into the container through the two pipes. After 5 minutes, Pipe A becomes blocked, so that water no longer comes in through Pipe A. Water continues to come in through Pipe B, until the container is full. Find the total length of time taken to fill the container. Give your answer in minutes and seconds. Hint: first find the fraction of the tank that each pipe fills in one minute.
solutionQuotes: the fraction filled by both pipes in five minutes
the fraction left to fill after 5 minutes
